basis: Defining cutaneous mucinosis and monoclonal gammopathy; myopathy in 30-79%. Dysphagia alone does not establish direct gut damage; documented hypoperistalsis is 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia occurs in 30-79%, but may reflect myopathy; direct gastrointestinal abnormalities and hypoperistalsis are reported in 5-29%.

basis: Skeletal-muscle dystrophy with common demyelinating peripheral neuropathy, estimated >30% across predominantly congenital cases; white-matter MRI changes alone would not qualify.

decisions.neurologic: involved: peripheral nerve demyelination with slowed conduction is common, especially in complete laminin deficiency; estimated >30% across the usual disease spectrum.

basis: Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; structural genu valgum occurs in 4/12 (~33%). Constipation and feeding difficulties do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: genu valgum is a structural skeletal abnormality reported in 4/12 (~33%); the supplied evidence does not establish that it is merely a transient postural finding.

basis: Sacral cutaneous hemangiomas are vascular endothelial tumors involving skin and blood vessels. Associated congenital abnormalities are unspecified.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hemangiomas arise from blood vessels, which fall within this axis; localized cutaneous vascular tumors need not cause systemic cardiovascular disease.

basis: Mediastinal smooth-muscle malignancy has no specified origin in an organ covered by these axes; mediastinal soft tissue is not locomotor connective tissue.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: smooth muscle and mediastinal soft tissue are outside the locomotor structures covered by this axis; skeletal-muscle origin is not established.

basis: Hereditary fibrinogen protein-folding/storage disorder causing predominantly glomerular amyloid deposition and renal failure; clinically damaging extrarenal involvement is uncommon.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hereditary fibrinogen amyloidosis is an inherited disorder of protein folding and deposition, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Dystonia/deafness define syndrome; immunodeficiency 80-99%. Oral clefts/achalasia 2/2; skeletal defects 2/2 and ocular damage 30-79% omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate and achalasia occur in 2/2; defining oral involvement is placed here because the three primary slots include neurologic, otologic and the immune mechanism.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at four-axis cap: kyphoscoliosis and skeletal malformations occur in 2/2, but neurologic, auditory, gastrointestinal and immune involvement take priority.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: supplied HPO explicitly reports immunodeficiency in 80-99%; an immunodeficiency requires this mechanism axis.

basis: Lysosomal glycoprotein degradation disorders; neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal dysostosis each affect an estimated >30% across major forms. Organomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal dysostosis and joint abnormalities occur across multiple major mucolipidosis and oligosaccharidosis forms, supporting an estimated frequency >30%.

basis: SRD5A3-related dolichol/glycosylation disorder with intellectual disability and cataracts; kyphosis and contractures occur in 3/3, placed in involved because of the primary cap.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: established SRD5A3-related defective dolichol synthesis and glycosylation constitute an inborn metabolic disorder, beyond a gene association alone.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: defining kyphosis and joint contractures occur in 3/3; placed here because metabolic mechanism, neurologic and ocular disease occupy the three primary slots.

basis: Congenital diaphragm and upper-limb defects; direct developmental pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in >30% of typical congenital diaphragmatic hernia, although syndrome-specific data are absent.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: developmental lung hypoplasia from congenital diaphragmatic herniation is common (>30% in the usual course); confidence is limited by absent syndrome-specific frequencies.
